newsitem.title: UK: AMP mulls Scotland move if wins ScotAm bid - paper.
newsitem.headline: AMP mulls Scotland move if wins ScotAm bid - paper.

text.p: Australian life insurer AMP is considering moving its Bristol-based subsidiary London Life to Scotland if its bid for Scottish Amicable is successful, according to The Scotsman newspaper.

The paper said on Thursday that AMP would use a base in Scotland to expand into Europe, and that it placed considerable importance on the Glasgow office of Scottish Amicable Investment Managers (SAIM).
The two other main contenders, Prudential Corp Plc and Abbey National Plc, are believed to have plans to downscale or close SAIM, the paper said.

Both Abbey and Prudential have said they want to grow the business in Scotland, but as their main operations are in England, both have said there are likely to be unqualified job cuts in areas of duplication.

The Scotsman said AMP understands that the key determinant in the contest will be price, but that the implied better job security it offers for Scottish Amicable staff may give it the edge against its competitors.
Scottish Amicable has 2,200 staff, most of whom are policyholders.
